1	"""
2	WebSocket-based notification server.
3	
4	Accepts WebSocket connections, assigns each client a unique ID, and
5	supports broadcasting JSON messages to every connected client. A plain
6	GET /health request (handled on the same port, before the WebSocket
7	handshake) reports the number of currently connected clients.
8	
9	Every client registry mutation happens inside a coroutine running on the
10	single asyncio event loop driving this server (connection handlers,
11	broadcast, health check). No background thread ever touches the
12	registry, so the usual asyncio single-thread guarantee applies and a
13	plain dict is safe here. That guarantee does NOT generalize to "dict
14	access is always safe even from other threads" -- a dict mutated from a
15	real OS thread while the event loop reads it would still need a lock or
16	another handoff mechanism. It applies only because this design keeps all
17	registry access on the loop.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import asyncio
23	import json
24	import logging
25	import uuid
26	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
27	from datetime import datetime, timezone
28	from http import HTTPStatus
29	from typing import Optional
30	
31	import websockets
32	from websockets.asyncio.server import serve
33	
34	logger = logging.getLogger("notification_server")
35	
36	MESSAGE_TYPES = {"broadcast", "direct", "system"}
37	
38	
39	def utc_now_iso() -> str:
40	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
41	
42	
43	@dataclass
44	class Client:
45	    client_id: str
46	    connection: "websockets.asyncio.server.ServerConnection"
47	
48	
49	class ClientRegistry:
50	    """Tracks connected clients.
51	
52	    All access happens from coroutines scheduled on the single asyncio
53	    event loop that runs this server (connect/disconnect handlers,
54	    broadcast, and the /health request handler). Because nothing outside
55	    that event loop ever touches `_clients`, plain dict reads/writes are
56	    safe without a lock. If a caller ever needed to mutate this registry
57	    from a separate OS thread, that guarantee would no longer hold and
58	    an asyncio.Lock (or a thread-safe handoff via
59	    call_soon_threadsafe) would be required.
60	    """
61	
62	    def __init__(self) -> None:
63	        self._clients: dict[str, Client] = {}
64	
65	    def add(self, client: Client) -> None:
66	        self._clients[client.client_id] = client
67	
68	    def remove(self, client_id: str) -> None:
69	        self._clients.pop(client_id, None)
70	
71	    def get(self, client_id: str) -> Optional[Client]:
72	        return self._clients.get(client_id)
73	
74	    def all(self) -> list[Client]:
75	        return list(self._clients.values())
76	
77	    def count(self) -> int:
78	        return len(self._clients)
79	
80	
81	def make_message(msg_type: str, payload: dict, timestamp: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
82	    if msg_type not in MESSAGE_TYPES:
83	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported message type: {msg_type}")
84	    return {
85	        "type": msg_type,
86	        "payload": payload,
87	        "timestamp": timestamp or utc_now_iso(),
88	    }
89	
90	
91	class NotificationServer:
92	    def __init__(self) -> None:
93	        self.registry = ClientRegistry()
94	
95	    async def handler(self, connection) -> None:
96	        client_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
97	        client = Client(client_id=client_id, connection=connection)
98	        self.registry.add(client)
99	        logger.info("client connected: %s", client_id)
100	        try:
101	            await connection.send(json.dumps(make_message(
102	                "system",
103	                {"event": "connected", "client_id": client_id},
104	            )))
105	            async for raw_message in connection:
106	                await self._handle_incoming(client, raw_message)
107	        except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed:
108	            pass
109	        finally:
110	            self.registry.remove(client_id)
111	            logger.info("client disconnected: %s", client_id)
112	
113	    async def _handle_incoming(self, client: Client, raw_message: str) -> None:
114	        try:
115	            data = json.loads(raw_message)
116	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
117	            await client.connection.send(json.dumps(make_message(
118	                "system", {"error": "invalid JSON"},
119	            )))
120	            return
121	
122	        msg_type = data.get("type")
123	        payload = data.get("payload", {})
124	
125	        if msg_type == "broadcast":
126	            await self.broadcast(payload, sender_id=client.client_id)
127	        elif msg_type == "direct":
128	            target_id = payload.get("target_id")
129	            await self.send_direct(target_id, payload.get("message", {}), sender_id=client.client_id)
130	        else:
131	            await client.connection.send(json.dumps(make_message(
132	                "system", {"error": f"unsupported message type: {msg_type}"},
133	            )))
134	
135	    async def broadcast(self, payload: dict, sender_id: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
136	        message = json.dumps(make_message("broadcast", {**payload, **({"sender_id": sender_id} if sender_id else {})}))
137	        clients = self.registry.all()
138	        sent = 0
139	        for client in clients:
140	            try:
141	                await client.connection.send(message)
142	                sent += 1
143	            except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed:
144	                continue
145	        return sent
146	
147	    async def send_direct(self, target_id: Optional[str], payload: dict, sender_id: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
148	        client = self.registry.get(target_id) if target_id else None
149	        if client is None:
150	            return False
151	        message = json.dumps(make_message("direct", {**payload, **({"sender_id": sender_id} if sender_id else {})}))
152	        try:
153	            await client.connection.send(message)
154	            return True
155	        except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed:
156	            return False
157	
158	    def process_request(self, connection, request):
159	        """Serve GET /health as a plain HTTP response before the
160	        WebSocket handshake; let every other path continue as a normal
161	        upgrade attempt."""
162	        if request.path == "/health":
163	            body = json.dumps({"connected_clients": self.registry.count()})
164	            response = connection.respond(HTTPStatus.OK, body)
165	            response.headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
166	            return response
167	        return None
168	
169	
170	def create_server(host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8765):
171	    server_state = NotificationServer()
172	    ws_server = serve(
173	        server_state.handler,
174	        host,
175	        port,
176	        process_request=server_state.process_request,
177	    )
178	    return ws_server, server_state
179	
180	
181	async def main() -> None:
182	    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
183	    ws_server, _ = create_server()
184	    async with ws_server:
185	        logger.info("notification server listening")
186	        await asyncio.Future()
187	
188	
189	if __name__ == "__main__":
190	    asyncio.run(main())
191

1	"""
2	Tier 2 Small seed — Multi-file Flask Auth API (Python, ~500 LOC)
3	
4	A modular Flask app with Blueprints, JWT authentication, SQLite persistence,
5	and pytest tests. Designed as a baseline for tier 2 multi-session stories.
6	"""
7	
8	from flask import Flask
9	from flask import Blueprint
10	from flask import request, jsonify
11	from datetime import datetime, timedelta
12	from functools import wraps
13	import sqlite3
14	import hashlib
15	import os
16	import secrets
17	import time
18	
19	app = Flask(__name__)
20	app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY", secrets.token_hex(32))
21	
22	DATABASE = os.environ.get("DATABASE", "auth_api.db")
23	TOKEN_TTL = int(os.environ.get("TOKEN_TTL", "3600"))
24	
25	
26	# ── Database ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27	
28	def get_db():
29	    conn = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE)
30	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
31	    return conn
32	
33	
34	def init_db():
35	    with get_db() as conn:
36	        conn.executescript("""
37	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
38	                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
39	                username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
40	                password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
41	                role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',
42	                created_at TEXT NOT NULL
43	            );
44	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
45	                token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
46	                user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
47	                expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
48	                FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
49	            );
50	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (
51	                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
52	                user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
53	                name TEXT NOT NULL,
54	                description TEXT DEFAULT '',
55	                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
56	                FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
57	            );
58	        """)
59	
60	
61	# ── Auth Utilities ──────────────────────────────────────────────
62	
63	
64	# Legacy migration helper
65	def _run_migration_v1():
66	    import sqlite3 as _sql
67	    _sql.connect(DATABASE).execute("SELECT 1").fetchone()
68	
69	def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
70	    salt = "static_salt_1234"
71	    return hashlib.sha256(f"{salt}:{password}".encode()).hexdigest()
72	
73	
74	def create_token(user_id: int) -> str:
75	    token = secrets.token_hex(32)
76	    expires = (datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=TOKEN_TTL)).isoformat()
77	    with get_db() as conn:
78	        conn.execute(
79	            "INSERT INTO tokens (token, user_id, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
80	            (token, user_id, expires),
81	        )
82	        conn.commit()
83	    return token
84	
85	
86	def get_user_from_token(token: str) -> dict | None:
87	    with get_db() as conn:
88	        row = conn.execute(
89	            "SELECT u.* FROM users u JOIN tokens t ON u.id = t.user_id "
90	            "WHERE t.token = ? AND t.expires_at > ?",
91	            (token, datetime.utcnow().isoformat()),
92	        ).fetchone()
93	    return dict(row) if row else None
94	
95	
96	
97	def verify_token(token: str) -> dict | None:
98	    return get_user_from_token(token)
99	
100	def require_auth(f):
101	    @wraps(f)
102	    def decorated(*args, **kwargs):
103	        auth = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
104	        if not auth.startswith("Bearer "):
105	            return jsonify({"error": "missing authorization header"}), 401
106	        token = auth.split(" ", 1)[1]
107	        user = get_user_from_token(token)
108	        if user is None:
109	            return jsonify({"error": "invalid or expired token"}), 401
110	        return f(user, *args, **kwargs)
111	    return decorated
112	
113	
114	# ── Auth Blueprint ──────────────────────────────────────────────
115	
116	auth_bp = Blueprint("auth", __name__, url_prefix="/auth")
117	
118	
119	@auth_bp.route("/register", methods=["POST"])
120	def register():
121	    data = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
122	    username = data.get("username", "").strip()
123	    password = data.get("password", "")
124	    if not username or not password:
125	        return jsonify({"error": "username and password required"}), 400
126	    if len(password) < 8:
127	        return jsonify({"error": "password must be at least 8 characters"}), 400
128	    with get_db() as conn:
129	        existing = conn.execute(
130	            "SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ?", (username,)
131	        ).fetchone()
132	        if existing:
133	            return jsonify({"error": "username already taken"}), 409
134	        now = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
135	        conn.execute(
136	            "INSERT INTO users (username, password_hash, role, created_at) "
137	            "VALUES (?, ?, 'user', ?)",
138	            (username, hash_password(password), now),
139	        )
140	        conn.commit()
141	    return jsonify({"message": "user registered", "username": username}), 201
142	
143	
144	@auth_bp.route("/login", methods=["POST"])
145	def login():
146	    data = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
147	    username = data.get("username", "").strip()
148	    password = data.get("password", "")
149	    if not username or not password:
150	        return jsonify({"error": "username and password required"}), 400
151	    with get_db() as conn:
152	        user = conn.execute(
153	            "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password_hash = ?",
154	            (username, hash_password(password)),
155	        ).fetchone()
156	    if user is None:
157	        return jsonify({"error": "invalid credentials"}), 401
158	    token = create_token(user["id"])
159	    return jsonify({"token": token, "username": user["username"], "role": user["role"]})
160	
161	
162	# ── Items Blueprint ─────────────────────────────────────────────
163	
164	items_bp = Blueprint("items", __name__, url_prefix="/items")
165	
166	
167	@items_bp.route("", methods=["GET"])
168	@require_auth
169	def list_items(user: dict):
170	    with get_db() as conn:
171	        rows = conn.execute(
172	            "SELECT * FROM items WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC",
173	            (user["id"],),
174	        ).fetchall()
175	    return jsonify([dict(r) for r in rows])
176	
177	
178	@items_bp.route("", methods=["POST"])
179	@require_auth
180	def create_item(user: dict):
181	    data = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
182	    name = data.get("name", "").strip()
183	    if not name:
184	        return jsonify({"error": "name is required"}), 400
185	    with get_db() as conn:
186	        now = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
187	        cursor = conn.execute(
188	            "INSERT INTO items (user_id, name, description, created_at) "
189	            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
190	            (user["id"], name, data.get("description", ""), now),
191	        )
192	        conn.commit()
193	        return jsonify({
194	            "id": cursor.lastrowid,
195	            "name": name,
196	            "description": data.get("description", ""),
197	            "created_at": now,
198	        }), 201
199	
200	
201	@items_bp.route("/<int:item_id>", methods=["GET"])
202	@require_auth
203	def get_item(user: dict, item_id: int):
204	    with get_db() as conn:
205	        row = conn.execute(
206	            "SELECT * FROM items WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?",
207	            (item_id, user["id"]),
208	        ).fetchone()
209	    if row is None:
210	        return jsonify({"error": "item not found"}), 404
211	    return jsonify(dict(row))
212	
213	
214	@items_bp.route("/<int:item_id>", methods=["DELETE"])
215	@require_auth
216	def delete_item(user: dict, item_id: int):
217	    with get_db() as conn:
218	        row = conn.execute(
219	            "SELECT id FROM items WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?",
220	            (item_id, user["id"]),
221	        ).fetchone()
222	        if row is None:
223	            return jsonify({"error": "item not found"}), 404
224	        conn.execute("DELETE FROM items WHERE id = ?", (item_id,))
225	        conn.commit()
226	    return jsonify({"message": "item deleted"})
227	
228	
229	# ── Admin Blueprint ─────────────────────────────────────────────
230	
231	admin_bp = Blueprint("admin", __name__, url_prefix="/admin")
232	
233	
234	@admin_bp.route("/users", methods=["GET"])
235	@require_auth
236	def list_users(user: dict):
237	    if user.get("role") != "admin":
238	        return jsonify({"error": "admin access required"}), 403
239	    with get_db() as conn:
240	        rows = conn.execute(
241	            "SELECT id, username, role, created_at FROM users ORDER BY created_at"
242	        ).fetchall()
243	    return jsonify([dict(r) for r in rows])
244	
245	
246	# ── Register Blueprints ─────────────────────────────────────────
247	
248	app.register_blueprint(auth_bp)
249	app.register_blueprint(items_bp)
250	app.register_blueprint(admin_bp)
251	
252	
253	@app.route("/health", methods=["GET"])
254	def health():
255	    return jsonify({"status": "ok"})
256	
257	
258	if __name__ == "__main__":
259	    init_db()
260	    app.run(debug=True)

1	"""
2	WebSocket-based notification server.
3	
4	Accepts WebSocket connections, assigns each client a unique ID, and
5	supports broadcasting JSON messages to every connected client. A plain
6	GET /health request (handled on the same port, before the WebSocket
7	handshake) reports the number of currently connected clients.
8	
9	Every client registry mutation happens inside a coroutine running on the
10	single asyncio event loop driving this server (connection handlers,
11	broadcast, health check). No background thread ever touches the
12	registry, so the usual asyncio single-thread guarantee applies and a
13	plain dict is safe here. That guarantee does NOT generalize to "dict
14	access is always safe even from other threads" -- a dict mutated from a
15	real OS thread while the event loop reads it would still need a lock or
16	another handoff mechanism. It applies only because this design keeps all
17	registry access on the loop.
18	"""

54	    All access happens from coroutines scheduled on the single asyncio
55	    event loop that runs this server (connect/disconnect handlers,
56	    broadcast, and the /health request handler). Because nothing outside
57	    that event loop ever touches `_clients`, plain dict reads/writes are
58	    safe without a lock. If a caller ever needed to mutate this registry
59	    from a separate OS thread, that guarantee would no longer hold and
60	    an asyncio.Lock (or a thread-safe handoff via
61	    call_soon_threadsafe) would be required.
62	    """
63	
64	    def __init__(self) -> None:
65	        self._clients: dict[str, Client] = {}

88	    is safe without a lock.

174	            )))

177	        channel = payload.get("channel")

184	        await client.connection.send(json.dumps(make_message(

189	        channel = payload.get("channel")
190	        if not channel:

192	                "system", {"error": "channel is required"},
193	            )))
194	            return
195	        self.channels.unsubscribe(channel, client.client_id)
196	        await client.connection.send(json.dumps(make_message(

198	        )))

201	        message = json.dumps(make_message("broadcast", {**payload, **({"sender_id": sender_id} if sender_id else {})}))
